title: דבי ר' ינאי

paragraphs: Rabbi Yannai’s school: Berakhot 32a; Shabbat 30b, 52b, 77b, 85b, 141b; Eruvin 77b, 82a, 95b; Yoma 65a, 86a; Sukkah 28b: Rabbi Yannai’s school says, and so forth; Rabbi Shimon says. This requires examination, for it puts them before Rabbi Shimon. Megillah 21a; Yevamot 113b; Ketubbot 15a; Kiddushin 57a; Gittin 15b; Bava Kamma 92a; Bava Metzia 103b, 105a; Avodah Zarah 19a, 62b; Zevachim 70b; Niddah 58a; Bereshit Rabbah, section 15; Eichah and Megillah. See Bereshit Rabbah, end of section 72, and Jerusalem Talmud, HaRoeh. Maimonides’ introduction to the Mishneh Torah writes that Rav received from Rabbi Yannai. Raavad writes against him: ‘It never happened and was never created.’ There is some evidence from Yevamot above, Rav according to Rabbi Yannai, although we find the reverse in Kirah 39b, end: Rabbi Yochanan said: Rabbi Yannai said: Rav said. It seems to me it should read Rabbi, for Rabbi Yannai often says in Rabbi’s name. On this broken-reed support, it seems to me Sheerit Yosef listed Rabbi Yannai among Rav’s students; by all opinions Rabbi Yannai was not Rav’s student. Rav was greater than he, for Rav belonged to Rabbi’s court in HaNizakin; this is contradicted by Yevamot above, Rav according to Rabbi Yannai. Resh Lakish in Rabbi Yannai’s name: Sukkah 17b, Meilah 18a, Bava Metzia 26b, Eruvin 11b, Gittin 60a, Oto VeEt Beno 82a, Niddah 3b, end. Kol Kitvei 119a: he wore fine clothes on Sabbath eve and said, ‘Come, bride’; Bava Kamma 32b. He told his sons: ‘Bury me neither in white nor in black’: Shabbat 117a as printed (the matching passage is 114a); Taanit 10a; Kiddushin 49b; Niddah 20a. Rabbi Yannai said: ‘They learn from what is spoiled, not from what is repaired’: Jerusalem Talmud, Moed Katan. But our reading attributes it to his son Rabbi Shimon; see his entry. Rabbi Yochanan was attached to Rabbi Yannai, and Rabbi Yannai to Rabbi Chanina: Bava Metzia 85b. Rabbi Yannai suffered somewhat with his eyes, as in Bava Batra. Surely the intended passage is Bava Batra 111a: Rabbi Yannai walked leaning on his attendant Rabbi Simlai’s shoulder. Rabbi Yehudah Nesia came toward him. His attendant told Rabbi Yannai: ‘The man coming toward us is handsome, and his cloak is handsome.’ Rashbam explains Rabbi Yannai was old and his eyes had begun to grow dim. ‘Feel Rabbi Yehudah Nesia’s cloak,’ and so forth. It requires examination whence Rashi knew his eyes dimmed from age. Shabbat 108b says he sent to Mar Ukva to send him some of Master Shmuel’s eye salve. He replied: ‘A drop of cold water put in the eyes in the morning, and washing the hands and feet in warm water in the evening, which also brightens the eyes, are better than all salves.’ It appears his eyes did not dim from age, for age-related weakness has no cure, as known from medical books. Rabbi Yannai said: ‘Tefillin require a clean body. Why did they not persist in them? Because of deceivers.’ Someone deposited with his fellow, and so forth. Rabbi Yannai wore them for three days after illness, because illness cleanses, and so forth: Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot, chapter 2, mishnah 3. Rabbi Yannai was Rabbi Ammi’s father-in-law: Midrash Chazit, first verse, and end of Jerusalem Talmud, Eruvin; see Rabbi Yannai bar Ammi above. That matter in Jerusalem Talmud, Shabbat, end of Kol HaKelim, lacks the word father-in-law. But at the beginning of Jerusalem Talmud, Gittin, chapter 2, Rabbi Yonah is a scribal error. Rabbi Yannai and Rabbi Yochanan: the law follows Rabbi Yannai, for he was Rabbi Yochanan’s teacher (Halikhot Olam 35a).

Since there are an earlier Rabbi Yannai and Rabbi Yannai Rabbah, understand and discern who spoke in the earlier Rabbi Yannai’s name and who in Rabbi Yannai Rabbah’s name. Rabbi Abba be-Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba and Rabbi Zeira asked Rabbi Yannai. Rabbi Avin said: Rabbi Yannai said. Rabbi Avin bar Kahana. Rabbi Oshaya said: Rabbi Yannai said, Ketubbot 79a, end. Rabbi Acha, Rabbi Chanina, and Rabbi Meyasha transmitted in his name: Midrash Eichah, on ‘The Lord rejected His altar.’ Rav Acha son of Rava transmitted in his name; this requires examination. Rabbi Ivo said: Rabbi Yannai said. Rabbi Ila transmitted in his name. Rabbi Inai said: Rabbi Yannai said. Rabbi Elazar said: Rabbi Yannai said. Rabbi Elazar ben Antigonos transmitted in his name. Rabbi Assi said: Rabbi Yannai said. Rabbi Ammi was his son-in-law; see above. Gamliel Zuga. Rav Dima said: Rabbi Yannai said. Rav Huna said: Rabbi Yannai said, Chullin 122b. Rabbi Yannai said: Rabbi Zeira said, Sukkah 50a, beginning. This requires examination: Rabbi Zeira was Rabbi Assi’s student; Rabbi Assi was Rabbi Yochanan’s student; Rabbi Yannai was Rabbi Yochanan’s teacher. Would he speak in his student’s student’s student’s name? Yet Rabbi Zeira asked him, above. Rabbi Zeira in the name of someone from Rabbi Yannai’s school: beginning of Tomnin. Rav Zeaira sent to Rabbi Yannai’s school: Jerusalem Talmud, Keitzad Mevarkhin, mishnah 1. Rabbi Chizkiyah transmitted in his name. In Rabbi Chiyya bar Vava’s name. He asked Rabbi Chiyya; see above. Rabbi Chila transmitted in his name. Rabbi Chanina Tortai said: Rabbi Yannai said. Rabbi Chanina was before him; Rabbi Yannai told him: ‘Go read your verse outside,’ Af Al Pi 56a, beginning. Rabbi Chanina the reader was before him. R.Y. ben Pazi [ר״י; provisionally Rabbi Yehudah] in his teacher Rabbi Yannai’s name, and so forth; Rabbi in Rabbi Yannai’s school’s name: Dinah’s original conception was male. Thus in Jerusalem Talmud, HaRoeh; the same matter in Bereshit Rabbah, end of section 72, has a changed reading, without R.Y. ben Pazi [ר״י; provisionally Rabbi Yehudah] in his teacher Rabbi Yannai’s name, nor ‘Rabbi in the school’s name,’ and so forth. Yehudah be-Rabbi Chiyya Rabbah was his son-in-law. Rabbi Yehudah Nesia came to him; see above. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi transmitted in his name: Jerusalem Talmud, Taraf BaKalpi. Rabbi Yehoshua bar Giddel. Rabbi Yochanan was his student. Rabbi Yonatan ben Amram was his teacher; see above. Rabbi Yonatan: Jerusalem Talmud, Kiddushin 1:7. Rabbi Yonatan ben Yosef was his colleague. Rabbi Yeili transmitted in his name. Rabbi Yannai, son of Rabbi Yannai the Elder’s son, transmitted in his name. Rabbi Yitzchak bar Yosef said: Rabbi Yannai said. Rabbi Yitzchak Chakula. Rabbi Mani bar Pattish transmitted in his name. He sent to Mar Ukva; see above. Rava transmitted in his name. Rav was his student; see above. Rabbi was his teacher; see above. Simlai was his attendant; see above. Resh Lakish transmitted in his name and disputes with him; see above. In Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel’s name: Sanhedrin 11a. His son Rabbi Shimon. Rabbi Shimon Berabbi: Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 6.
